faq: Why is a nautical mile longer than a land mile?

They were born from different ideas: the statute mile is land-survey history (5,280 feet), while the nautical mile is one arcminute of the Earth's latitude — about 6,076 feet. Navigation kept the one tied to the chart.
Yes. One international nautical mile is exactly 1,852 metres by definition, so every result here is exact arithmetic, not an estimate.
How do I convert kilometres back?
Divide by 1.852 — or use the Kilometers to Nautical Miles Converter, the dedicated reverse lane.
What is a knot in km/h?
One knot is one nautical mile per hour: exactly 1.852 km/h, about 1.15 mph. Ten knots is a bicycle's pace; thirty is a fast ferry.
Do pilots and sailors use the same nautical mile?
Yes — the international nautical mile is shared by IMO and ICAO convention, which is precisely why the unit survived into aviation.
How many nautical miles around the Earth?
The equator is about 21,600 nautical miles — sixty for every one of the 360 degrees, the definition closing its own circle.
